Subject: Request to onboard RelayCore (telemetry relay) as a subprocessor

Hi David,

Quick note — FinoSys is evaluating RelayCore to take over telemetry relay for our EU + US pilots.  They will receive limited telemetry (non-PII traces + routing metadata) and will be acting as a transit relay; we expect <1% of traffic to be routed in the pilot.

Can Redwood add RelayCore to the subprocessor roster and share the residency/export trail info you require?  They provided an onboarding package (attached) including a short SOC summary and a network egress spreadsheet. Sophie (ops@finosys.com) is looped for logistics.

Attachments: relaycore-onboarding.pdf

Wed like to start the pilot the week of Aug 30, so the compliance/attestation check needs to be quick.

Best,
Sophie Martin
Head of Integrations, FinoSys
Sophie.Martin@finosys.com


From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@finosys.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to onboard RelayCore (telemetry relay) as a subprocessor

Kim, Priyom — Sophie just asked us to add RelayCore as a telemetry relay for FinoSys pilot.  Key asks from my side before we can approve:

- Confirm where RelayCore will store logs and whether any transient traces cross EU->US.
- Confirm KMS jurisdiction for any persisted metadata (is key material in EU?).
- Provide SOC2 type II report or summary and PCI/PII exclusion statement.
- Network egress list (IP ranges & countries) so we can map to our export controls.

Sophie attached their package but I want to be concrete on what we need to hand back to FinoSys. Can you:
  1) validate the SOC2 summary (quick pass),
  2) confirm whether RelayCores env meets our EU residency/egress constraints, and
  3) draft the DPA addendum language wed need if this subprocessor is accepted.

Ill hold with the roster addition until compliance confirms. Sophie — if RelayCore can provide the IP list and the KMS jurisdiction we can move faster.

Thanks,
David
Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks David — quick triage below after a first pass on the attachment.  Ill need RelayCore to confirm the items highlighted before we sign off:

Checklist (required items)
- SOC2: we need either a full Type II report or an attested summary from an external auditor. The attached PDF is a vendor summary; not sufficient on its own.
- Export trace: country-level egress matrix + ASN/IP ranges (we require IP ranges for routing policy).
- KMS: confirm whether encryption keys are customer-controlled (bring-your-own-key) or vendor-managed; list KMS provider and key jurisdiction.
- Data minimization: explicit statement that no customer PII/credentials are persisted.
- Subprocessor cascade: list any downstream subprocessors RelayCore uses for CDN/ingest.

Operational asks for FinoSys (acceptable format)
- Provide network-egress.csv (columns: cidr, country, purpose) — we need this for legal mapping.
- Provide a short attestation email from RelayCores security contact confirming the KMS jurisdiction and PII exclusion.
- If SOC2 is not available within 5 business days, provide compensating controls (onsite audit window or escrow for EU pilot).

Attachments (internal): RelayCore_contact_sheet.csv (vendor contact + security POC)

Sophie — if you can push RelayCore to share the network-egress.csv and a security contact attestation today, we can usually produce a DPA addendum draft within 48 hours.

Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Appreciate the quick review, Kimberly.  Per RelayCore security: see attached SOC summary and network egress CSV.  High-level answers below and Ive asked their security lead (cc: ops@finosys.com) to follow up with the formal attestation and DocuSign envelope.

- KMS: vendor-managed keys hosted in EU for EU-region instances; US-region keys are hosted in AWS KMS (us-east-1). No customer BYOK for the pilot.
- Persistence: RelayCore retains only aggregated telemetry for 14 days; no customer credentials or tokens are persisted (they confirmed in writing).
- Downstream: they use EdgeCacheX (CDN) for transient routing; EdgeCacheX is listed in the network-egress CSV.
- SOC2: attached is a current summary and auditor contact; full Type II available on request (3-5 business days).

Attachments: relaycore-soc2-summary.pdf, network-egress.csv
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/RelayCore_Onboarding_12345

If compliance signs off, FinoSys will route a test subset to RelayCore starting Aug 31.  Let me know if you need anything else today.

Best,
Sophie
